sections.h2: Ways to sell a house in Racine
sections.html:
Selling in Racine means picking among a traditional listing, handling it yourself, or accepting cash from an investor or home buyer. Three things steer the choice: the state of the house, whether tenants are inside, and how fast you need the proceeds.

  • Standard listing. Exposure to buyers with mortgages comes with inspections, appraisals and repair requests. Get the commission and any other seller-paid charges written down.
  • For sale by owner. Pricing, tours, the condition report and the deed filing become your tasks, and they take time.
  • Cash sale. With no lender involved, closing can move faster. Weigh offers by what you net after fees, when closing happens and which repairs the buyer wants.

Tenants in the house, or code items you know are open, make the permit and tenant sections below worth reading before you commit to any buyer.

About 77,908 people live in Racine, in 31,970 households that average 2.39 people. Owners occupy 60.2 percent of homes. The median owner-occupied home is worth $166,500. Mortgage holders pay a median of $1,398 a month, renters a median gross of $1,033, and the median household earns $57,740. Racine is 22 miles south of Milwaukee and 60 miles north of Chicago.

Medians cover the whole city. A recent roof and a clean permit file put a house in a different spot from one with repairs waiting. Price from recent sales near you.

The Racine Unified School District administers the public schools, and rusd.org explains school choice and enrollment. Parents shopping for a house often ask about boundaries and choice options. Point them to the district. Do not guess.

Building, heating, plumbing, electrical and zoning codes all fall to the Building Inspection Department, reachable at 262-636-9464. Its permit page includes applications for roofs, siding, fences, garages and sheds, decks and pergolas, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, razing and an occupancy permit. Before closing, ask whether your sale triggers an occupancy permit and whether any permit from earlier work remains open.

Buyers who want nightly rentals face extra steps. A stay shorter than 29 consecutive days falls under the state's tourist rooming house rules. The city requires a permit from its Public Health Department, an inspection each year before any guest arrives, and room tax under Racine Ordinance 90-55. Permits run on a July 1 to June 30 year. Short-term rentals pay Wisconsin sales tax at 5 percent in Racine, unless taxable sales stay under $1,000 in a calendar year. Questions go to Environmental Health at 262-636-9203.

With tenants in the house, the city's guidance is for landlords to complete a signed check-in and check-out form. Tenants then have seven days after move-in to report any other defects. A landlord who skips this written process weakens his or her position in a dispute over conditions, unless a government inspector verified them earlier. Give those records to your buyer. The Fair Housing Office takes questions at 262-636-9595.

A seller of a home with one to four units owes the buyer a finished condition report no later than 10 days after acceptance, under Wis. Stat. 709.02. The form covers structural and mechanical systems, environmental matters, wells, septic systems and storage tanks, taxes, special assessments and permits, and land use. Miss the deadline and the buyer may rescind in the two business days after day 10. Should an answer change before the buyer accepts, Wis. Stat. 709.035 calls for an amended report. Wis. Stat. 709.01 excuses court-appointed fiduciaries who never occupied the home, plus transfers exempt from the transfer fee.

sections.h2: Transfer fee and recording at the county
sections.html:
Under Wis. Stat. 77.22 the grantor pays 30 cents per $100 of value. At the Racine County Register of Deeds, recording any document costs a flat $30, and every document has to pass a checklist.

Racine County recording checklist
RequirementWhat it means
PartiesGrantor and grantee named, with the grantor's signature notarized or authenticated
PropertyComplete legal description and the parcel identification number
DrafterName of the person who prepared the document, plus a return address
FormatLegible text that follows Wisconsin margin and layout guidelines

Find the office at 730 Wisconsin Avenue. It is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm and accepts documents dropped off, mailed or filed electronically. Questions go to (262) 636-3208 or rod@racinecounty.gov. The county's page posts a quit claim deed form, but let an attorney or title company confirm which deed suits your sale.

Gather these before you accept an offer. Racine buyers and title companies tend to want the parcel identification number, which also belongs on the deed. Add the permit record for earlier work, any occupancy permit paperwork, and your mortgage payoff figure. For a rental, pull the lease and the check-in and check-out forms. If a buyer plans nightly stays, have the Public Health Department and Environmental Health numbers ready so the buyer can start the permit conversation early.

An heir can sell. What changes is the paperwork, which follows from how title passed. Wis. Stat. 77.25(11) exempts a transfer by will, descent or survivorship from the transfer fee, and recording a Termination of Decedent's Property Interest (HT-110) costs $30 at the county. A court-appointed fiduciary who never lived there does not need to complete the condition report. The probate court or an attorney can confirm which category you are in.

sections.h2: Order of steps once you have an offer
sections.html:
Begin with the condition report, which is due 10 days after acceptance. Answer every section, structural systems through land use. Then phone Building Inspection about open permits or an occupancy permit. Tenants in place? Gather the lease and the signed check-in and check-out forms. Finally, get an attorney or title company to draft the deed, file the transfer return online and deliver the deed with its recording fee to 730 Wisconsin Avenue.

A cash buyer can take away the appraisal and the loan approval. It cannot take away the report, the return or the recording, so plan for each.

faqs.q: What do I do about tenants when I sell a Racine house?
faqs.a: Read the lease first and ask an attorney how a sale affects it. The city recommends signed check-in and check-out forms listing the condition of major components, and tenants have seven days to report additional defects. Give your buyer copies and call the Fair Housing Office at 262-636-9595.

faqs.q: Is a permit needed if my buyer plans nightly rentals?
faqs.a: Yes. Stays under 29 consecutive days require a Tourist Rooming House permit from the Public Health Department, an inspection before the first guest, room tax and Wisconsin sales tax, unless taxable sales stay under $1,000 a year. Permits run July 1 through June 30.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer fee on a Racine sale?
faqs.a: You do, as grantor, at 30 cents per $100 of value under Wis. Stat. 77.22. The register of deeds collects it when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded for a Racine house?
faqs.a: At the Racine County Register of Deeds, 730 Wisconsin Avenue, Racine, WI 53403. Drop it off, mail it, or let a title company file it electronically. Recording is a flat $30, and the transfer return must be filed online first.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Racine house I inherited?
faqs.a: Yes, though the paperwork depends on how title passed. A transfer by will, descent or survivorship owes no transfer fee, and a court-appointed fiduciary who never lived in the house is excused from the report. Confirm with the probate court or an attorney.
